correctness.rationale: Each completed pair consumes two private goods; attaining K forces a perfect matching of colored edges and hence a monochromatic assignment per alternating component. With monochromatic components EF1 is exactly |2s−K|≤1. In the no-balanced-subset case a crossing component admits a contiguous 2a+1 versus 2(k−a)−1 split that loses exactly one pair; its two within/between bundle valuations agree in reverse order, making the allocation EF1. Exhaustive independent enumeration of all matching pairs and allocations through 10 goods corroborates every case, but infinite scope follows from the proof.

value.rationale: For the natural two-agent boundary of the motivating pair-complement setting, the theorem replaces a known impossibility at four items with a complete all-size quantitative efficiency frontier: every optimal EF1 allocation loses at most one pair, and a graph component subset-sum condition characterizes when no loss is necessary. The polynomial constructive proof identifies exact structural, nontrivial thresholds for complement-based fair allocation.
